releases: B1: coverage by registered month and partition label (every month listed, so a gap shows as 0); records with no anchor; records with no label
B2: counts by population code per cell, which reconcile to the record count
B3: counts by class per cell and label

B4: per cell, model and label: scored orders, fills, fills by kind, fills within 1 s and 2 s of t, fills by kind in the after-the-hour seconds, fills in a batch that moves the market from OPEN to not OPEN, orders ended by the pull and by the lapse, and the fill rate; and the fill counts per model of each class that is not scored

B5: per cell and model, the two labels pooled: the sample SD of gross g over filled orders and its symmetric ranges q95 - q05, q90 - q10 and q75 - q25, under measurement.part_and_rest; per cell: the SD of gross g over all scored orders, quantiles of the queue at t, and seconds to fill as quantiles
B6: per cell and model: the detectable effect on the test label (statistics.rule), printed with: under independence; clustering makes it larger
blind_pass.rule: The blind pass runs first, over the whole input, and gives only what releases lists; the partition labels are shown apart only for counts. People read it. The registered pass runs once, at the same code commit and backtest sources, and only with the blind receipt of this registration, split file and input; nothing in this file may change between the two passes, since any change is a new sha256. Each pass is one entry in the study ledger, written after the read and before any output: a look for a blind pass, at most two per study, and the one registered entry for the lineage on the test label. Of an outcome the blind pass gives only statistics that a shift leaves as they are: the sample SD and the symmetric ranges. They keep a group's spread but not its location or direction.
withholds: every mean, median, raw quantile, sign, interval, test, label and selection of an outcome
any SD of net_closed or net_held: the kink at 0 leaks the location (inference)
any statistic by price band or half-year
any per-market or per-runner row, market id or selection id

data.duplicates: A record of the registered tier is keyed by its market id alone; one id twice in that tier refuses the run (input:<archive sha256>:duplicate_market), so no market is decided or counted twice. Keep the PRO archive in its own data root. A record of another plan is coded plan_not_registered.
data.files: The runner reads the split file beside the studies/ folder that holds this registration, and the rule files in rules/ beside that folder; in the repository these are research/ and research/rules/. Each file's sha256 must equal the one named here. A name is a plain file name, never a path.
data.month: the UTC month of the first-published marketTime

partitions.rule: Every record gets the label of its race date from the split file (partition.Split.label). The race date is the Europe/London calendar date of the first-published off. A record whose label is not one of the two named here is coded partition_not_registered and its file is never opened. Every tally is keyed by label. The selection receives the explore label's tallies and the test label's counts only. One pass reads both labels, and every index record already holds BSP and results, so the split is kept by code paths and tests, not by separate files.

data.source: every archive ingested and indexed under one data root (archive.py, market_index.py), each market from its index record's primary member, replayed with the index's own fold, checked against the record at every decision time (replay.view_from_fold) and read on, message by message, to the last pull time of the cells that reached the book; nothing later is parsed, and no other source stands in

traded_volume.rule: As lp-v1 (research/studies/lp-v1.json, data.traded_volume.rule), folded by the same code (lp.TradedFold): PRO rc.trd counts backer's stake x 2, so a matched backer's stake of s shows as a rise of divisor x s; atb and atl sizes are backer's stake, with no divisor. Messages sharing a pt are one batch. A batch is open when the market status in force before its first message is OPEN. A rise counts as traded volume only in an open batch, and only when that batch also carries an atb or atl entry at that price for that runner (lp-v1's rule, an inference its blind pass checked before the off). So the batch that suspends the market still credits the trades it carries, the batch that reopens it does not, and a rise in a batch that is not open is never counted later. The settlement-zeroing frame is counted and ignored. Some trd updates are currency restatements, sent a few seconds after each whole hour, Monday to Friday; after_the_hour_s is how many seconds after the hour the diagnostics set apart.

decided_by: Yu, 2026-11-11: named the rule files, the data split and the ledger, gave the OK for this offline replay on the 2015-16 PRO year, and said the account is on Basic 2%. The design (three fill models, the two nets, the split of the year, the labels) is lab-Claude's, from the lab's research round of 2026-11-11 and its three reviews. Each pass over real data needs Yu's OK for that pass.

diagnostics.rule: Counts only, in both passes; they change no code, class or statistic, and one that shows a rule wrong leads to a fix, a new registration and a new blind pass. Per cell, model and label: fills within each of within_s seconds of t, which a slower connection could change; fills by kind whose pt lies in the first data.traded_volume.after_the_hour_s seconds after a whole UTC hour on a Monday to Friday; fills in an open batch that left the market not OPEN; orders ended unfilled by the pull and by the lapse. Per order, over (t, pull time] and its runner (trd_counts): rises counted as trades; rises not counted, in an open batch outside the after-the-hour seconds, at a price that was the best back or best lay just before the batch (many of them beside the counted rises would mean the counting rule drops trades and the fill counts understate); rises in a batch that was not open. Scored BSPs that are whole hundredths and those that are not. Null values undefined, by reason. Cells that passed a flag gate with no value for the flag at t.

exposure.fresh_on_test: Fresh on PRO-V: the fill rates, and the gap between filled and unfilled orders.

lines.lp-v1: Join-leg mark-outs at 10 minutes before the off, and fill counts (docs/lp-study.md).
lines.movement-v1: Taker NCLV of the favourite's best back by time, with intervals and SDs (docs/movement-study.md); on the lab also means by price band, field size and late-move cell, and raw tick quantiles.
lines.p0: The year counts as inspected from P0's first run (docs/movement-study.md). Its run started two variants; their outcome metrics stay on the lab (docs/backtest-plan.md).
lines.suite-counts: Whole-year counts of in-play markets and of markets with a removal. Counts, not locations.

exposure.not_fresh_on_test: Not fresh on PRO-V: the level of g, on either side of the split. For the LAY file, mean g over all placed orders is minus movement-v1's taker gross on the whole year, PRO-V dates included. For the BACK file the best lay was never released, but the window, the band and the gates come from the same whole-year results.
exposure.printed_with_every_label: The level of g was known from the whole year. Only the gap is new.

family.rule: Candidates: the 6 cells. Tested family: one primary cell per rule file (selection), so m is the number of rule files, whether or not a rule file gets a primary. One-sided tests of a mean above 0 on the test label, at alpha in all, Holm inside the family. No conditional cell: the test label cannot confirm one at plausible sizes.

fill_models.rule: We do not know our place in the queue, so every order is judged three times; the models differ only in the queue. queue = queue_fraction (numerator, denominator) x the size shown at t at the order's price on its own side (a LAY rests on atb, a BACK on atl): optimistic is the front of the queue, central is behind half the size shown, pessimistic is behind all of it (lp-v1's join rule). A fill is judged when a pt batch is complete, for the batches after t up to and including the pull time. The first kind that holds, in the order of kinds: trade_through, the batch counts a rise at a price beyond the order's (below a LAY, above a BACK), whatever its size; quote_cross, the batch carried an image or a ladder key for the runner and the size then shown on the opposite side at or through the order's price (atl at or below a LAY, atb at or above a BACK) is at least the stake; volume_at_price, the counted volume at the order's own price has risen since t by at least divisor x (queue + stake), so GBP 2 needs a rise of 4 at the front and 2 x (queue + 2) behind a queue. One fill, in full, at the order's own price. Nothing published at or before t fills. No fill is credited from a batch that is not open (data.traded_volume.rule). Once inPlay was true before a batch, a lapse order is no longer judged. The cross test needs the stake only, where lp-v1 needed queue + stake: by price-time priority an opposing order can come to rest at or through our price only after every order ahead of ours there is matched or pulled, so asking for the queue again would count it twice. Inference, not checked on real files.

grid.rule: A cell is one rule file at one of its times: two rule files x three times = 6 cells. The times and pull times are the rule files' own: placed at off - 600 s or off - 300 s and pulled at off - 120 s, or placed at off - 120 s and pulled at off - 10 s; t = the first-published scheduled marketTime + at_s. Each cell is an independent hypothetical: its order is our only order in the market, never a re-entry or a book shared with another cell's order. The view at t holds every message published at or before t, the batch at t included; the order rests from that batch with no delay, through every message published after t up to and including the pull time. It is never re-priced. A lapse order also ends when the market turns in play before its pull time.

bsp_ends.rule: The stream appears to cut BSP to two decimals (docs/data-audit.md: a 2017 sample, unchecked on 2015-16), so the true BSP lies between the value as written and that plus step. Every g and net is computed twice: against BSP as written and against BSP + step. The kill end is the figure that favours the order (LAY: BSP + step; BACK: as written); the claim end is the other. If at least whole_hundredths_share of the scored orders' BSPs are whole hundredths, kills read the kill end and claims the claim end; else the as-written figure decides alone. Both are printed either way. BSP is never snapped to a tick.

bsp_valid_if: the market's final status is CLOSED and its last bspReconciled is true
the runner is listed at the end with final status WINNER or LOSER
its final bsp is a finite number above 1 (the index keeps none below 1.01)
measurement.classes_rule: Every order rulefile.decide returns is a placed order and ends in exactly one class, the first that applies, from facts that do not depend on a fill. The first five are movement-v1's (movement.measure), for the selected runner and the runners ACTIVE and listed at t: outcome_unknown when the member was not read whole or a runner's later state cannot be assessed; void_own_runner_removed when the selected runner was removed after t; post_decision_removal when another of those runners was; result_revised_after_close; missing_bsp when bsp_valid_if fails. Then stream_malformed_after_placement when a ladder entry, a trd entry or an rc runner id published after t and up to the pull time could not be read. Else scored. A suspension, an early off or a revised schedule after t does not drop an order: the fill rules handle them and the tables count them. Only scored orders enter a statistic; every other class stays in the placed counts with its fill counts per model. Market-level void cannot be seen in these files and is never inferred.
measurement.commission_source: Yu, 2026-11-11: the account is on Basic 2%
measurement.deciding_net: The kill reads net_closed: a kill on the kinder net is also a kill when held. The claim and the measurement label read net_held, for both rule files: a rule file has no closing order, and a GBP 2 BACK cannot be closed at BSP (a BSP lay has a GBP 10 minimum liability, fact F38), so for the BACK net_closed is a bound no real order reaches.
measurement.g: Per GBP 1 of backer's stake, positive is good for the order: a BACK at P scores g = P / BSP - 1 and a LAY at L scores g = 1 - L / BSP. Every placed order has a g at its own price, filled or not.
measurement.intent_to_treat: Per cell and partition label, over scored orders: (1) the mean over filled orders, per model, of g, net_closed and net_held; (2) the mean g over all placed orders, each valued at its own price, filled or not, with no fill model; (3) the value per placed order, net_held when filled and 0 when not, per model; (4) the gap, mean g over filled minus mean g over unfilled, per model, as a CR1 contrast by race date.
measurement.mid: the mid at t is (best back + best lay) / 2 of the selected runner's quote at t when its best back is below its best lay and they are at most null.max_spread_ticks CLASSIC ticks apart; the registered pass prints it against BSP beside the placed mean
measurement.net_closed: g - commission_rate x max(g, 0), unrounded: the order closed at BSP at equal stakes. It is the kinder net, always at or above net_held.
measurement.net_held: the order held to the result, unrounded: for a BACK g - commission_rate x (P - 1) / BSP (contract p1's NCLV); for a LAY g - commission_rate x (1 - 1 / BSP).
measurement.part_and_rest: A mean, SD, range or interval for a part of a group is given only if the part and the rest each hold statistics.min_values values. If a model's unfilled part is smaller, that model's filled figures are replaced by the all-placed figures and flagged filled_is_all_placed, in tables, bounds, labels and blind SDs. Without this, two means would give one order's g.
measurement.removals: No re-pricing. An order with any other runner removed after t is classed post_decision_removal and is not scored; docs/betfair-facts.md has no reduction-factor entry. The removals come when the best-informed traders act, so this exclusion leaves out some of the fills most likely to be adverse and flatters the result by an unknown amount, as lp-v1 said of its own (docs/lp-study.md). The size of each excluded class is printed beside every mean.
measurement.unit: a fraction of the backer's stake; tables print 100 x g as points of stake. These are not lp-v1's implied-probability points, which are differences of 100 / price.

not_measured: latency: the orders rest from the batch at t with no delay; the diagnostics count the fills within 1 s and 2 s of t, which a delay could change
partial fills: every fill is all or nothing
virtual (cross-matched) prices, which the files' ladders exclude
queue position: no tier shows it, so three fill models stand in for it
removals: classed, never re-priced by a reduction factor
a closing order, and the penny rounding of its commission
the kill numbers K1 to K8 of the 2026-11-11 research round

null.label: close-v1/null/{market_id}/{at_s}/{rule_id}
null.rule: The random-time null, a gate on claims only. For every placed order a time u is drawn at placement, uniform over the whole milliseconds of (t, pull time], with metrics.HashStream(seeds.null, label); only scored orders' values are read. The null value is the mid at u (every message published at or before u) against BSP, signed for the side: BACK m_u / BSP - 1, LAY 1 - m_u / BSP. It is undefined, and counted by reason, for the first that applies: member_unreadable (the member could not be read through u), market_not_open (the status at u is not OPEN), in_play (inPlay is true at u), not_two_sided (no best back below a best lay), spread_above_max (the best lay is more than max_spread_ticks CLASSIC ticks above the best back). It is read only for a primary whose other claim conditions all hold, over that primary's pessimistic fills on the test label. It blocks when it or the main mean over the same orders cannot be computed, or when its absolute mean is at least fraction_of_main x the absolute main mean and its own two-sided p is below alpha or undefined (movement-v1's rule). A blocked claim prints claim_blocked_by_placebo and the label falls through. The null never kills: as a kill it would fire on any clearly negative mean. A null that does not block is not proof: fills crowd towards the pull time and a uniform u does not.

population.codes_rule: Per cell, every index record gets exactly one code, the first that applies in this order, or issued. Codes reconcile to the record count per cell. The first twelve are movement-v1's history gates and market predicates (movement.market_code), read against the rule file's market block from what was published at or before t; the field size is the rule file's own row, not a gate here. Then partition_not_registered (data.partitions). Then bsp_market_false when the rule file gates bsp_market and bspMarket as of t is exactly false; a missing value passes and is counted (diagnostics). A record whose cells all have a code by now is never opened. Then ladder_malformed when a ladder entry, a trd entry or an rc runner id published at or before t could not be read. Then the code rulefile.decide gives for the view at t, in its order: the rule file's market rows (market_not_open, too_few_active_runners), the selector's codes (no_priced_active_runner, favourite_tie), the rule file's runner rows (best_back_out_of_range, depth_below_min, spread_not_1_or_2_ticks) and no_reference_price. Then price_off_ladder when the order's price is not a CLASSIC ladder price. A when row of a rule file may not use one of the harness's own codes (the first twelve, partition_not_registered, a flag code, ladder_malformed, price_off_ladder, issued), and every when code must be in this list.
population.price_ladder: CLASSIC assumed for GB and IE horse-racing WIN markets, as movement-v1 and lp-v1 assume: index v1 does not track priceLadderDefinition, so every order price is checked against the CLASSIC ladder instead
population.quotes: PRO's atb and atl, folded as movement-v1 folds them (movement.LadderFold): price-keyed [price, size] deltas, where a size of 0 deletes that price and an empty list empties that ladder; a null value changes nothing; an image (img true) replaces every runner's ladders. A runner's best back is the highest price of its back ladder and its best lay the lowest of its lay ladder, each with its size, as the file wrote them. The view a rule file reads (resting.view_of) holds the runners ACTIVE and listed at t, each with its best back, the size there, its best lay and the CLASSIC ticks between them; market_open is 1 when the status as of t is OPEN and inPlay as of t is not true. Quotes are not cleared while the market is not OPEN: the rule files' market_open row refuses a decision then, and no fill is credited from a batch that is not open.
population.source: the two rule files (data.rules): movement-v1's favourite gates plus market_open, which movement-v1 only counted; not a pilot contract

releases: T5: per cell, for the explore label (exploratory) and the test label (not tested, unadjusted, except the primaries): the figures of measurement.intent_to_treat with n, race dates, SD and CR1 95% interval, at both BSP ends; the mid at t against BSP; the size of each class that is not scored beside every mean
T7: half-years: every cell on the explore label; the primaries only on the test label, all three models
T8: the selection: the eligible cells and the chosen cells
T9: per primary: the test, Holm, both bounds, the gap of measurement.intent_to_treat with its interval, the null, the label
T10: sensitivity: the filled mean without the fills in the first second after t; the quantiles of the sum of 1 / BSP per market
registered_pass.rule: Only the tests and bounds verdicts.rule names decide anything; every other interval is descriptive. A group below statistics.min_values gives counts only, and a test below its gates is not tested. There is no table by price band.

selection.rule: Mechanical, fixed before any pass. For each rule file: among its cells with at least statistics.min_tested_values scored explore_model fills on statistics.min_tested_race_dates race dates on the explore label, and at least as many test_model fills and race dates on the test label (counts only), the primary is the cell with the highest mean net_held over the explore_model fills on the explore label, at the claim end. A tie goes to the later time. No such cell: that rule file has no primary and still counts in family.m. The function receives the explore label's tallies and the test label's counts, nothing else.

statistics.rule: A group with fewer than min_values values gives counts only, in either pass: no SD, quantile, range, mean or interval. A test, a bound or a selection needs min_tested_values values on min_tested_race_dates race dates, and each rule checks the gate of the model it reads. The one-sided p for a mean above 0 is 1 - student_t_cdf(mean / SE, G - 1), with CR1 by race date (uncertainty.rule). A p-value, test, flag or label is printed only for a primary on the test label; the other test-label rows print n, race dates, mean, SD and an interval headed not tested, unadjusted; explore-label rows carry no p, and each table prints its number of cells c and sqrt(2 ln c). Quantiles are by nearest rank: with n sorted values, the q quantile is value ceil(q x n), counted from 1. The blind pass gives the quantiles of an outcome only as the symmetric ranges q(1 - a) - q(a), so quantiles must hold 1 - a beside every a. Floats are rounded to 6 places, quantiles and ranges to 4. The SD is the sample SD, with n - 1. The detectable effect on the test label is (t(detectable_level; G - 1) + t(power; G - 1)) x SD / sqrt(N), from the pooled SD and the test label's fill count and race dates; it is under independence, and clustering makes it larger.

summary: Registered offline measurement, not a backtest contract. It asks whether a resting GBP 2 order on the favourite, placed 10, 5 or 2 minutes before the off and pulled before it, gets a price that beats BSP once only the orders that would fill are counted. Two frozen rule files say what is ordered (data.rules): a BACK at the best lay price and a LAY at the best back price, on GB and IE horse-racing WIN markets rebuilt from the free 2015-05..2016-04 Betfair Historical Data PRO files. An order here is a simulated intent; nothing can reach an exchange. Every order is judged under three fill models: front of the queue, behind half the size shown, behind all of it. The score is the fill price against BSP per pound staked, before and after 2% commission, for all orders placed and for the orders that filled, at both ends of the stream's two-decimal BSP. The year is split by race date (data.split): PRO-D to look around, PRO-V for one test. A blind pass gives counts and spreads only. One registered pass picks one primary cell per rule file on PRO-D by a rule fixed here and tests only those on PRO-V. Every pass is written into the study ledger before any number comes out. A good result is a reason to try something live at small stakes, never proof; a bad result under the front-of-queue model, on the whole year, closes the idea. It changes no existing source file, nor lp-v1 or movement-v1; adding fills.py, resting.py and resting_study.py to the backtest package changes the engine's source descriptor and certificate key again, so any later run-backtest needs certify-engine.

uncertainty.rule: As movement-v1 and lp-v1: m = sum(x) / N, SE^2 = G / (G - 1) x the sum over race dates g of (the sum over values i in g of (x_i - m))^2 / N^2, and the interval m +/- t x SE with t the (1 + confidence_level) / 2 quantile of Student's t with G - 1 degrees of freedom; fewer than min_clusters race dates give the mean without an interval. The race date is the Europe/London calendar date of the first-published off. The three times of one market and both rule files share a race date, so their dependence stays inside one cluster.

verdicts.prediction: Signed by lab-Claude on 2026-11-11, before any pass: no primary is an edge_candidate; the pessimistic mean net_held on PRO-V is below 0 for both rule files; the labels are measurement_pilot_candidate or unresolved, with unresolved the likelier because the held net decides. kill_optimistic on a rule file ends that side of the idea.
verdicts.printed_with: PRO 2015-16: a kill gate and a prior, never confirmation
verdicts.rule: One label per primary cell, the first that applies. (1) kill_optimistic: on the explore and test labels pooled, the optimistic model has statistics.min_tested_values fills on statistics.min_tested_race_dates race dates and the kill bound of mean net_closed, mean + t(kill_level; G - 1) x SE at the kill end, is below 0. A kill spends no alpha. (2) underpowered: the pessimistic model on the test label has fewer fills or race dates than those gates. (3) edge_candidate: on the test label, at the claim end, on net_held: the one-sided test of the pessimistic mean is rejected under Holm at family.alpha; the mean is above 0 under all three models; the pessimistic mean is above 0 in H1 and in H2, each with half_year_min_fills or more fills; and the null does not block. (4) measurement_pilot_candidate: on the test label, the pessimistic lower bound of mean net_held, mean - t(lower_bound_level; G - 1) x SE at the claim end, is above minus pilot_floor_below_zero: 600 fills at GBP 2 would then cost at most about GBP 18 in expectation. (5) unresolved. A low mean alone never prints a kill, and neither does the null. The pessimistic fill rate is printed beside every label. Every label is printed with printed_with, exposure.printed_with_every_label, both nets, both BSP ends and any filled_is_all_placed flag.
